Paraguay’s Next Development Chapter
news.summary_en: Paraguay today has the potential to transform its development story, but it will require close cooperation with international partners to make the best use of its advantages.

news.title: Amid Iran War Tensions, Energy Market Resilience Wears Thin
news.summary_en: Fresh attacks on energy infrastructure in the Middle East may push regional leaders to build the first post-U.S. security arrangement for the Strait of Hormuz. As U.S. voters head to the polls in a few weeks, an expensive war linked to affordability concerns will be top of mind.

news.title: The U.S.-China Summit: Too Big and Too Small to Fail
news.summary_en: Scott Kennedy argues that although the Trump-Xi summit will likely extend the current period of stability, the gap between the convening’s limited ambitions and the growing challenges facing the world points to a growing vacuum of global leadership.

news.title: Is the U.S. Banking System Ready for a Post-Quantum Future?
news.summary_en: Sultan Meghji argues that the hardest cryptographic deadline facing U.S. banks is being set by SWIFT and foreign supervisors, not Washington. Adversaries are harvesting encrypted financial traffic now. Three of the four fixes require no new statutory authority.

news.title: The AI Industry Is Coalescing on “Pacing the Frontier.” Will It Actually Change Anything?
news.summary_en: Over the past week, frontier labs, policymakers, and the U.S. public have reached remarkable consensus around calls to pace AI development. What now? Aalok Mehta outlines the four steps government and industry must take to translate the current moment into durable change.

news.title: Building and Using a U.S. Polar Defense Industrial Base
news.summary_en: As great power competition intensifies, expanding the U.S. polar industrial base can bolster U.S. defense capabilities, support the peaceful governance of the Arctic and Antarctic, and create new economic opportunities at home.

news.title: Six Charts to Explain the Global Energy Crisis
news.summary_en: The conflict with Iran continues to redraw the energy map. Six charts show how major producers and consumers are stabilizing markets through reserve releases, lower imports, and increased U.S. production of oil, gas, and helium.

news.title: Don’t Slow Down AI Development—Speed Up Benchmarking
news.summary_en: Ben Jensen and Yasir Atalan argue that the United States should stop debating how fast to build and start funding independent benchmarking—through NSF, NIST, and university policy labs.

news.title: Beyond the Memory Cycle: AI, HBM, and the New Semiconductor Shortage
news.summary_en: AI-driven demand for high-bandwidth memory is reshaping the semiconductor memory market, creating shortages across industries and raising new questions about U.S. supply chain resilience, investment, and the risk of future overcapacity.
